## Beginner Budget Dinner: Garlic Tomato Pasta with Fried Eggs

A simple, filling dinner for 2 using one saucepan and one frying pan. It uses common pantry ingredients, stays mild, and comes together fast.

## What You’ll Make

**Time:** 20–25 minutes
**Serves:** 2
**Skill level:** Beginner
**Flavor:** Mild, savory, budget-friendly

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

### Ingredients
- 200 g pasta, any shape
- 2 eggs
- 2 tbsp cooking oil or butter
- 2 cloves garlic, finely chopped or crushed
- 1 small onion, finely chopped
- 1 can chopped tomatoes or 3 medium tomatoes, chopped
- 1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1/2 tsp dried oregano or mixed herbs
- 1 tsp sugar, optional, to balance acidity
- 1 small handful grated cheese, optional

### Equipment
- 1 saucepan
- 1 frying pan
- Spoon or spatula
- Colander or lid for draining pasta

## Simple Cooking Steps

### 1) Cook the pasta
- Fill the saucepan with water and bring it to a boil.
- Add a pinch of salt and the pasta.
- Cook until tender, following the package time.
- Save a small cup of the pasta water, then drain.

### 2) Make the tomato sauce
- Heat 1 tbsp oil in the frying pan over medium heat.
- Add onion and cook for 3–4 minutes until soft.
- Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
- Add tomatoes, salt, pepper, herbs, and sugar if using.
- Simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.

### 3) Fry the eggs
- Push the sauce to one side of the pan or use the same pan after transferring sauce to a bowl.
- Add the remaining oil.
- Crack in the eggs and fry until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked to your liking.
- For a softer yolk, cook 2–3 minutes; for firmer yolks, cook a little longer.

### 4) Combine and serve
- Add the drained pasta to the sauce and toss well.
- If it looks dry, add a splash of the saved pasta water.
- Divide between 2 plates or bowls.
- Top each serving with a fried egg.
- Add cheese if you like.

## Beginner Tips
- Keep the heat medium, not high, so the garlic does not burn.
- If the sauce tastes too sharp, add a tiny bit more sugar.
- If you do not have canned tomatoes, fresh chopped tomatoes work fine.
- You can add frozen peas or a little spinach if available.
